archetype.name: Dual-Threat (raw, big-arm)
archetype.definition: A 6-foot-5, 236-pound third-year backup whose legs and middle-of-the-field arm show up in flashes, but whose processing, timing on short throws and feel for pressure are still unfinished.

report.headline: Sack-prone backup with a real intermediate arm; Dallas's defense gives him room
report.take:
Joe Milton III is Philadelphia's third starting quarterback of the year. Jalen Hurts started most of the early weeks and Tanner McKee took Weeks 6 and 8. Milton has started Weeks 9 and 11, splitting a low-scoring loss to the Giants and a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh. That is two starts and 70 dropbacks, so everything here is a sketch. The sketch is consistent, though. He holds the ball, takes sacks at a rate that ranks 54th of 55 (15.4%), and loses expected points on the throws that are supposed to be easy. His -0.282 EPA per dropback is 49th of 55, and his -12.64 CPOE is 52nd.

The odd part of his profile is where the damage comes from. Throws under 10 air yards have cost -0.297 EPA a play with a CPOE of -19.6. Screens and swings behind the line (-0.527 EPA, no successful plays on 8 attempts) have been especially bad. Throws of 10 to 19 yards are the opposite: 69.2% completions, +0.446 EPA, a 69% success rate. He sees and hits the window over the linebackers. What he hasn't shown is the rhythm of the quick game, and the quick game is exactly what is supposed to protect a young quarterback from the rush. Deep, his arm hasn't connected yet: one completion on 7 attempts.

The sacks are the cost of that unfinished processing, not of his scrambling. He has 6 scrambles for 50 yards at +0.372 EPA apiece, and the legs are a real asset: 35.5 rushing yards a game ranks 2nd among qualifiers. But a pressure-to-sack rate of 58.3% (45th of 45) on a fairly ordinary 19.4% pressure rate means he is turning pressure into sacks rather than into scrambles. Third down is where it shows most. He faces 8.5 yards to go on average, converts 21.7%, and has lost 13.4 EPA there, which is most of his season's damage. He has also thrown zero interceptions, and that is notable for a quarterback this raw. He has been conservative with the ball in the air (16.4% aggressive throws) and has paid for it in sacks and checkdowns that die short.

Week 11 was cleaner as a passer. He got the ball out in 2.63 seconds rather than 3.12, took 3 sacks instead of 7, and posted -5.0 passing EPA versus -13.3. His legs disappeared, though (5 carries, 7 yards). He has the job for now, but McKee was estimated as a limited participant with his ribs. So this is an audition: two or three more starts that look like Week 11 with a touchdown or two attached would keep him in the chair.

strengths.title: Hits the intermediate window
strengths.body: On throws of 10-19 air yards he completes 69.2% at +0.446 EPA with a 69% success rate. That is the area where his size and arm let him drive balls past underneath defenders. It comes from 13 attempts, so it's a hint rather than a fact, but it's the clearest sign of an NFL-caliber skill in his sample.

strengths.title: Legs keep drives breathing
strengths.body: His 35.5 rushing yards a game rank 2nd among quarterbacks. His scrambles have been efficient (+0.372 EPA each) where his dropbacks have not. The Week 9 output (9 carries, 64 yards) faded to 5 for 7 against Pittsburgh, so the volume is game-dependent, but the athletic floor is real and gives him fantasy relevance his passing doesn't.

strengths.title: No interceptions yet
strengths.body: Zero picks in 55 attempts is the best mark among qualifiers. Part of that is a careful approach (16.4% aggressive throws), and he did put the ball on the ground with two turnover-worthy fumbles. Expect some interceptions to arrive with more volume, but caution has been a deliberate part of his game.

concerns.title: Pressure becomes sacks
concerns.body: A 15.4% sack rate is 54th of 55, and the pace17 projection is 85 sacks. That isn't a protection disaster: he's pressured on only 19.4% of dropbacks. The problem is that 58.3% of those pressures end in sacks, the worst rate in the league. This reads as a young quarterback holding the ball while reading the field rather than a cost of extending plays, and it's the single biggest thing he has to fix. Week 11 (3 sacks, 2.63s time to throw) is the first evidence he can.

concerns.title: The easy throws aren't easy
concerns.body: Passes under 10 air yards have produced -0.297 EPA with a -19.6 CPOE, and throws behind the line have produced -0.527 EPA with no successful plays. The quick game isn't bailing him out of anything. It isn't all on him: his targets on these plays have struggled too, with DeVonta Smith at -0.414 EPA per target and lead back Elijah Mitchell at -0.479. Accuracy and timing on short throws usually improve with reps, but they're also what a coaching staff judges a backup on.

concerns.title: Third downs sink drives
concerns.body: He converts 21.7% of third downs and has lost 13.4 EPA on them. Part of that comes from the 8.5 yards to go he faces on average, which itself is the product of first- and second-down sacks and short-throw failures. It ties into an offense ranked last in success rate. Until the early downs improve, third down will stay a graveyard.

trend.note: Both starts were below average, in different ways. Week 9 was a sack-filled mess (7 sacks, -13.3 passing EPA) rescued by 64 rushing yards. Week 11 was a cleaner, quicker passing game (3 sacks, -5.0) with almost nothing on the ground. That's progress as a passer, but on two games it isn't yet a trend.

nextGame.headline: Worst defense in football, a likely deficit, and a short week
nextGame.body:
Dallas ranks 32nd in defensive EPA and 30th against the pass. It also bleeds on exactly the throws Milton has botched: 0.185 EPA allowed on short passes, 28th. It allows quarterbacks 276 yards a game (30th) and 20.5 PPR points (29th). Deep, it has been sturdier (8th), so this sets up as a day to live underneath and in the intermediate zone rather than to chase his arm. The Cowboys' offense is 3rd in EPA and the Book has Dallas favored by 8.5 with a 47.5 total. If the game goes to script, Philadelphia will be throwing more than it wants to, and volume will come regardless of efficiency. The catch is the pass rush: Dallas's 6.7% sack rate is only middling, but against the league's most sack-prone passer, middling is enough to stall drives.

Availability shapes this on both sides. Dallas is thin in the back seven: corner DaRon Bland and safety Jalen Thompson are on IR, safety P.J. Locke is out with a concussion, linebacker Jaishawn Barham is out, and Dee Winters was estimated as a non-participant. That is a lot of coverage missing for a young quarterback to exploit. On Philadelphia's side, Dallas Goedert (shin) and Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) are questionable. Goedert has been Milton's most productive target at +0.524 EPA per target, and with Dontayvion Wicks on IR, losing him would narrow the menu further. Barkley's status matters for the checkdowns and the run game. McKee's ribs matter most of all: if he's cleared on a four-day turnaround, Milton's hold on the job gets shakier.

keyMatchups.title: Short passing versus a leaky underneath
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows 0.185 EPA on short throws, among the league's worst, and Milton has lost -0.297 EPA a play on throws under 10 air yards. Something has to give. With two starting safeties and a linebacker out for Dallas, this is the best chance he'll get to make the quick game work.

keyMatchups.title: His sack habit versus Dallas's rush
keyMatchups.body: Dallas's sack rate (6.7%, 14th) is average, but Milton converts pressure to sacks at the league's worst rate. A short week for a backup leaves little time to install answers. If he gets the ball out like he did against Pittsburgh, the sack total should land nearer 3 than 7.

keyMatchups.title: Game script forces volume
keyMatchups.body: Dallas's offense ranks 3rd in EPA, and Philadelphia is an 8.5-point underdog. Milton has averaged only 27.5 attempts in close, low-total games, and trailing should push that higher, along with the yardage that comes with it.

nextGame.watch: How quickly he gets rid of the ball on early downs. If his sack count stays at three or fewer against this secondary, his first 200-yard game and first touchdown are in play.

restOfSeason.body:
Two things are likely to hold: the legs, and a sack rate well above league average. Even with improvement, his pressure-to-sack habit and a team offense ranked 29th in EPA won't flip in a few weeks. What should regress upward is the touchdown column. Zero passing TDs on 55 attempts, with just one red-zone throw, says more about how few chances this offense has created than about a true talent level. Interceptions should also start to appear as volume grows. A fair expectation is roughly 170-220 passing yards with 25-35 on the ground, plus a touchdown every game or two, assuming he keeps the job.

That assumption is the biggest unknown. McKee is limited with rib trouble and has already started twice this year, and the dossier doesn't explain Hurts's absence after Week 7. Milton is starting on borrowed time, and his week-to-week value depends as much on the depth chart as on his own play. If he keeps Week 11's quicker release and the intermediate game keeps working, he can be a serviceable fill-in with fantasy value tied to his rushing. If the sacks return to Week 9 levels, the job won't stay his.
swingFactors: Tanner McKee's rib recovery and the starting job
Whether the quicker Week 11 release sticks
Dallas Goedert's availability with Wicks on IR

confidence.note: Two starts, 70 dropbacks, no career baseline, and a job that could change hands any week.
